source.title: Implicit Self-Regularization in Deep Neural Networks: Evidence from Random Matrix Theory and Implications for Learning
source.authors: Charles H. Martin; Michael W. Mahoney

record.file_problem: None; the supplied text contains the full paper.
record.tranche_reason: The study varies batch size and measures training and test accuracy, testing the large-batch generalization-gap claim with a different model and setup. It also measures spectral properties alongside performance.
record.gate_note: The paper varies batch size in MiniAlexNet and reports accuracy trends and spectral measurements. Results cited from other work are not extracted as rows.
record.test_reason: The study varies batch size and reports its own held-out accuracy results for MiniAlexNet on CIFAR-10, bearing on V5 in a new model setting. Loss-based early stopping means this is not an established fixed-epoch comparison. The study is not an original source for V5.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the batch-size conclusion: the authors attribute improved test accuracy with smaller batches to stronger implicit self-regularization. Their broader conclusion is that trained weight spectra exhibit distinct regularization phases, including heavy-tailed behavior in modern networks. The proposed causal explanation goes beyond the reported spectral and accuracy covariation.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses a scaled-down AlexNet on CIFAR10 and measures accuracy and spectral statistics across batch sizes; the version summarizes results across image classifiers and language models under fixed epoch budgets.
record.method_sensitivity: Batch size changes test accuracy and the measured Stable Rank and MP Soft Rank; the reported FC1 and FC2 ESD phase patterns also differ by layer.

fits_no_version.finding: Stable Rank and MP Soft Rank decrease with smaller batches while test accuracy increases.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Spectral rank measures covary with batch size and test accuracy in MiniAlexNet; this does not test magnitude-aware sharpness.

record.problems: The batch-size accuracy values are presented in a figure without numeric values in the text. The study uses MiniAlexNet on CIFAR10 and does not report uncertainty for the batch-size results.
record.rows_left_out: No additional version-linked results were reported in extractable text. Dropout and weight-norm accuracy curves appear in Figures 26 and 25, respectively, but the text does not state their held-out accuracy outcomes.

untested.parts: No own comparison of fitting random labels versus generalizing on natural labels.
No width sweep beyond the width needed to interpolate.
No controlled convolutional versus fully connected classifier comparison.
No adaptive optimizer versus SGD comparison.

Strictly equal realized epoch budgets; language models; longer-training remedies; learning-rate scaling and warmup; compensatory normalization or regularization changes; matching small-batch accuracy with an adapted recipe.

A with-versus-without-dropout accuracy comparison appears in Figure 26, but its direction and magnitude cannot be read from the supplied text. Training-set-size dependence, excessive-dropout underfitting, and joint removal with weight decay under augmentation are not established.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance, its relationship to generalization gaps at similarly low training loss, and ranking against norm and margin measures.
No removal of highly memorized examples followed by retraining.

record.verdict_notes: Figure 26's dropout comparison is already declared in rows_left_out, so it is not an undeclared missing result. Its caption alone cannot justify a V6 verdict. Missing fixed-epoch control is an untested condition, not evidence challenging or limiting V5.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Network width beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD and optimizer tuning.

Language models; fixed epoch-budget comparisons; learning-rate scaling with warmup; normalization or regularization changes that compensate for large batches; other classifiers matching small-batch accuracy within the same epoch budget.

Dropout effects on held-out error by training-set size and dropout level; joint removal of dropout and weight decay under data augmentation. The text shows accuracy curves but does not describe their dropout-specific outcomes in words.
Magnitude-aware weight perturbations, comparisons against norm- and margin-based measures, and correlations with the train-test gap.
Removing memorized examples and measuring subsequent test accuracy.

rows.subject: MiniAlexNet
rows.size_stated: Scaled-down AlexNet; FC1 is 4096 × 384, FC2 is 384 × 192, FC3 is 192 × 10.
rows.stage_stated: Trained on CIFAR10; up to 100 epochs, with early stopping on total loss.
rows.operation_detail: Varied training batch size from 500 down to 2.
rows.baseline: Batch size 32 is the baseline setup; test accuracy values are figure only.
rows.value: Figure only; text says test accuracy increases for extremely small batch sizes, then gradually decreases as batch size increases.
rows.note: The text describes the trend but gives no per-batch accuracy values. It also says both training and test accuracy decrease for larger batch sizes.
rows.check: Section 7 explicitly reports declining test accuracy as batch size increases, so partial understates the reported direction. Exact accuracies cannot be recovered from the supplied figure captions. Record the loss-based early stopping and unspecified realized epoch counts; equal epoch budgets are not established. Section 6.1 gives a nominal baseline batch size of 32, whereas the Section 6.2 baseline referenced by Section 7 uses 16.

rows.subject: MiniAlexNet
rows.size_stated: Scaled-down AlexNet; FC1 is 4096 × 384, FC2 is 384 × 192, FC3 is 192 × 10.
rows.stage_stated: Trained on CIFAR10; up to 100 epochs, with early stopping on total loss.
rows.operation_detail: Varied training batch size from 500 down to 2.
rows.measure: Stable Rank and MP Soft Rank
rows.baseline: Batch size 32 is the baseline setup; values are figure only.
rows.value: Figure only; both ranks systematically decrease with decreasing batch size, as test accuracy increases.
rows.note: These spectral measures are not the magnitude-aware sharpness measure specified in V7.
rows.check: The reported spectral trend is clear, but neither Stable Rank nor MP Soft Rank measures any version's named effect. In particular, these are not magnitude-aware sharpness measures and cannot establish V7.

relationships.condition: MiniAlexNet on CIFAR-10, batch sizes 2–500, fixed nominal learning rate and loss-based early stopping within a 100-epoch cap
relationships.reason: R1 reports decreasing test accuracy as batch size increases; training accuracy also declines above approximately 100. This supports the batch-size penalty in this recipe, while equal realized epoch budgets remain unverified.
relationships.display_finding: Unverified results suggest that test accuracy declined with larger batches. With early stopping, it is unclear whether the runs used the same number of epochs.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
